conditional_card.text: Given today's reading of Realised vol, trailing 21d (decile 1 of its own expanding history), the historical odds of a drawdown worse than 5% in the next 21 trading days were 18.0% (n = 1486) against 35.3% unconditionally (n = 6338). Over the SAME buckets the mean forward return was 1.04% conditional against 1.28% unconditional -- i.e. this gauge tells you about risk and tells you close to nothing about return. That is the whole point of it.

accumulating.note: The implied leg accumulates forward one NSE trading day at a time (vistas/evolve_jobs/optionchain_n50.py has no backfill path by design). Until it reaches 60 aligned days, no percentile is shown.

crp.definition: Option-implied average pairwise correlation of the NIFTY 50 (backed out of the NIFTY ATM implied vol against the constituents' ATM implied vols, free-float-weighted) minus the realised average pairwise correlation of the same 50 members' daily returns over the trailing 21 trading days. A positive gap means index options price stocks as moving together more than they actually have.
crp.method: Implied leg from data/vol/implied.json (vistas/vol_implied.py, which refuses to emit a value below 80% of index weight covered by an ATM IV); realised leg from data/vol/realized.json (vistas/vol_realized.py). Joined on EXACT date -- a gap is only counted on a day both legs printed.

crp.title: Correlation risk premium -- implied vs realised CORRELATION
crp.why: It is the signal Kyser asked to percentile-rank. The history does not exist yet, and this block says so with a counter rather than inventing one.

vrp.definition: India VIX (what NIFTY index options price for the next 30 calendar days, annualised %) minus the annualised realised volatility of the NIFTY 50 total-return index over the trailing 21 trading days. Both legs are in volatility POINTS, so the gap reads directly as 'implied was N points richer than realised'.
vrp.method: Data: India VIX from data/World Data PX till Sep 3, 2026.csv column '^INDIAVIX'; NIFTY 50 TR from data/Indices Data TR till Sep 2, 2026.csv column 'NIFTY 50'. One row = one NSE trading day, exact-date join (no forward-fill). Realised vol = sqrt(252 * mean(r^2)) over the trailing 21 daily log returns -- the zero-mean variance-swap convention. Percentile = 100 * (count of history <= today) / n, inclusive, n stated.

1y.label: 1y
1y.reason: coarse: n = 246 is enough for a low/mid/high band but not a point percentile (floor for that is 250)

vrp.title: Variance risk premium -- implied vs realised VOLATILITY
vrp.why: It answers the exact question asked of the correlation gap -- how expensive is implied risk relative to what actually materialised, and where does that sit historically -- but on a leg with 18 years of history instead of one day.

Every forward-return test was judged against the exact circular-rotation null, which keeps each signal's persistence intact and destroys only its pairing with the future. 3 test(s) cleared that null and the family-wide correction and then broke on the crisis kill-tests: disp21__fret63 (the sign flips between disjoint eras); vix__decile_mean_ret_63d (the gap changes sign between disjoint eras; and it dies once the 2008-09 and 2020 crisis windows are removed (ex-crisis gap 3.78, rotation p 0.06979)); vrp_exante__decile_mean_ret_21d (it dies once the 2008-09 and 2020 crisis windows are removed (ex-crisis gap 1.23, rotation p 0.05443)). notes: WHAT THE TWO GAPS ARE. A 'gap' here is the price of risk minus the risk that actually showed up. The VOLATILITY gap (left) is India VIX -- what NIFTY index options charge for the next 30 days -- minus the volatility the index has actually realised over the last 21 trading days, both in annualised percentage points. Today it is 5.98 points: implied 11.59 against realised 5.61. Over 4532 trading days from 2008-03-03 to 2026-09-02 this gap has averaged 2.876 points and been positive on 84.2% of days. The stronger version of the same fact needs the FORWARD leg: comparing India VIX with the volatility that then actually materialised over the next 21 days, implied exceeded it on 80.7% of 4512 days (average 3.032 points). Insurance is normally sold above its eventual cost, which is why the premium exists at all. Today's reading sits at the 82.1-th percentile of the full history (n = 4532).

READ THE GAP WITH BOTH LEGS IN VIEW. A wide gap can mean insurance got expensive OR that the market went quiet underneath it. Right now India VIX is 11.59 and realised vol is 5.61 -- the ratio is 2.065. Check the percentile of each leg on the tiles above before calling the premium rich.

WHY THE CORRELATION GAP HAS NO PERCENTILE. The correlation gap (right) is the same idea one level down: what options price for how much the 50 stocks move together, minus how much they actually have. The implied leg needs an ATM implied vol for enough of the index by weight, and the full-universe capture job began banking only recently: 23 dates captured, 0 clearing BOTH the 80%-weight coverage gate and the same-expiry horizon gate, and 0 of those line up with a same-day realised reading. (19 date(s) are refused by the horizon gate alone: NIFTY has weekly expiries and single stocks do not, so the capture was pricing a 5-day index vol against a 26-day basket -- that ratio is not a correlation. The capture now requests the constituents' own expiry; the series restarts from the first matched day.) A percentile needs a distribution; with fewer than 60 aligned days there is none, so this panel shows a counter instead of a number. On the measured NSE calendar (248.6 trading days a year) a coarse low/mid/high band becomes available around 2026-12-01 and a real percentile around 2027-09-06. Anything rendered before then would be decoration.

HOW EVERY p-VALUE BELOW WAS COMPUTED. These forward windows overlap -- today's next-21-day return shares 20 of its 21 days with tomorrow's -- and every signal is highly persistent. An ordinary t-statistic assumes neither and badly overstates significance on this data. So each test is judged against the EXACT circular-rotation null: the signal is rotated against the target through all n rotations, which keeps the signal's persistence and its exact distribution intact and destroys only its pairing with the future. p = the share of rotations at least as extreme as the real one. 60 tests were run; at a 0.1 false-discovery rate the family-wide cutoff is p <= 0.036465 and 25 survive (26 had a raw p below 0.05, against 3.0 expected by luck alone).

Given today's reading of Realised vol, trailing 21d (decile 1 of its own expanding history), the historical odds of a drawdown worse than 5% in the next 21 trading days were 18.0% (n = 1486) against 35.3% unconditionally (n = 6338). WHAT THIS IS NOT. None of this is a buy or sell call, and nothing here is sized or traded. The volatility and drawdown relationships are measured on a single index over one 26-year sample containing two dominant crisis episodes (2008-09 and March 2020); a leave-one-episode-out check is the right next step before anything here is used to size exposure. The realised correlation and dispersion series are computed on the CURRENT NIFTY-50 membership applied backwards, so they carry a survivorship tint. Every percentile on this panel prints its own n; if you cannot see an n, the number is not a percentile.
